Editorial inferences for the Final Project (concept graph, note split of the specification)

a.value: 'AI-based software other than CS50’s own (e.g., ChatGPT, GitHub Copilot, Bing Chat, et al.)'

b.value: 'AI-based software other than CS50’s own (e.g., ChatGPT, Claude, Copilot, Gemini, et al.)'

discrepancies.note: Both are 'e.g.' lists; w99-n04 quotes each page's list as it stands and does not merge them.

discrepancies.topic: Final-project AI exception missing from the honesty page

a.value: 'For your final project (and your final project only!) it is reasonable to use AI-based software other than CS50’s own'

b.value: lists such use as 'Not Reasonable' with no final-project exception

discrepancies.note: The project page is the more specific rule for the final project; w99-n04 states the exception only for the final project and keeps the honesty page's rule for everything else. Human confirmation suggested.

discrepancies.topic: Group work vs the honesty page

a.value: groups of one or two classmates are allowed, each contributing equally

b.value: 'Splitting an assessment’s workload with another individual and combining your work' is Not Reasonable

discrepancies.note: The project page explicitly allows groups for the final project only; elsewhere the honesty rule applies.

a.value: FAQ 'Why did I not pass my final project?' speaks of the 'README or DESIGN file'

b.value: the spec requires only README.md (named exactly that)

discrepancies.note: The package follows the spec: README.md only. The FAQ wording is probably from an older edition (inference).

a.value: 'at least 70% on each of this course’s problem sets as well as its final project'

b.value: 'at least 70% on each problem you submit … as well as on the course’s final project'

discrepancies.note: Neither page gives a per-criterion rubric for the final project; the package does not invent one.
Both URLs serve the same 2026 page; sources.json records both.

discrepancies.topic: Version control not taught on the project page

a.value: mentions only GitHub usernames, the submit50 login and uploading to the cs50/problems/2026/x/project branch of github.com/me50/USERNAME

b.value: Week 10 names Git as a tool for version control

discrepancies.note: w99-n03 links Week 10 for Git and does not teach git commands beyond what the official pages state.

discrepancies.topic: No grading rubric or word minimum

a.value: 'in the neighborhood of 750 words is likely to be sufficient' and 'several hundred words'

discrepancies.note: No official hard minimum or rubric exists; the checklist marks the 750-word figure as guidance, not a rule. The checklist's word counter is a self-check only.
